docs.title: biosqi
docs.text:
Explainable signal-quality assessment for biomedical recordings.

biosqi divides ECG, PPG, or EEG recordings into windows, computes transparent signal-quality indicators (SQIs), and returns:

  • a calibrated 0–100 usability score for each window;
  • a boolean mask suitable for downstream processing;
  • evidence for likely artifacts such as clipping, flatline, baseline wander, mains interference, and poor periodic consistency;
  • machine-readable JSON/CSV and a local interactive dashboard.

docs.title: Scope and safety
docs.text: biosqi measures properties of a recording. It does not diagnose a patient, determine whether a physiological pattern is normal, or replace review by a qualified clinician. The bundled model is validated on the datasets stated in Validation; performance may not transfer to a different sensor, population, acquisition protocol, or artifact distribution.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. Evidence before labels. Every quality decision exposes the indicator values that contributed to it.
  2. Calibration before confidence. A score is presented as a probability only when its calibration procedure and validation population are stated.
  3. No hidden preprocessing. Sampling rate, profile, window length, overlap, threshold, and model version are included in every report.
  4. Reproducible claims. Published metrics are generated by benchmarks/run_all.py from public datasets.

Continue with the Quickstart.

docs.title: analyze(recording, *, window_seconds=None, step_seconds=None, threshold=0.5, model=None, include_partial=True)
docs.text:
Analyze every channel and aggregate each window conservatively by median.

Scores are calibrated estimates from the selected model, not guarantees of clinical usability. The threshold is an application policy and should be validated for the intended downstream task.

Source code in src/biosqi/analysis.py 
def analyze(
    recording: Recording,
    *,
    window_seconds: float | None = None,
    step_seconds: float | None = None,
    threshold: float = 0.5,
    model: FusionModel | None = None,
    include_partial: bool = True,
) -> AnalysisResult:
    """Analyze every channel and aggregate each window conservatively by median.

    Scores are calibrated estimates from the selected model, not guarantees of
    clinical usability. The threshold is an application policy and should be
    validated for the intended downstream task.
    """

    if not 0.0 <= threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError("threshold must lie in [0, 1]")
    profile: SignalProfile = get_profile(recording.signal_type)
    window_length = profile.window_seconds if window_seconds is None else window_seconds
    step_length = profile.step_seconds if step_seconds is None else step_seconds
    fusion = load_default_model() if model is None else model
    warnings: list[str] = []
    window_results: list[WindowResult] = []
    for window in iter_windows(
        recording,
        window_length,
        step_length,
        include_partial=include_partial,
    ):
        channels: list[ChannelResult] = []
        for name, values in zip(recording.channel_names, window.data, strict=True):
            indicators = compute_indicators(values, recording.sample_rate, profile)
            invalid_count = sum(not indicator.valid for indicator in indicators)
            if invalid_count:
                warnings.append(
                    f"window {window.index}, channel {name}: "
                    f"{invalid_count} indicator(s) unavailable"
                )
            prediction = fusion.predict(indicators)
            channels.append(
                ChannelResult(
                    channel=name,
                    score=prediction.raw_score,
                    calibrated_score=prediction.calibrated_score,
                    indicators=indicators,
                    artifacts=attribute_artifacts(indicators, fusion),
                )
            )
        channel_tuple = tuple(channels)
        raw_score = float(np.median([channel.score for channel in channel_tuple]))
        calibrated_score = float(np.median([channel.calibrated_score for channel in channel_tuple]))
        window_results.append(
            WindowResult(
                index=window.index,
                start=window.start,
                stop=window.stop,
                start_seconds=window.start_seconds,
                stop_seconds=window.stop_seconds,
                score=raw_score,
                calibrated_score=calibrated_score,
                usable=calibrated_score >= threshold,
                channels=channel_tuple,
                artifacts=_aggregate_artifacts(channel_tuple),
            )
        )
    if not window_results:
        warnings.append("recording contains no samples")
    return AnalysisResult(
        source=recording.source,
        signal_type=recording.signal_type,
        sample_rate=recording.sample_rate,
        channel_names=recording.channel_names,
        n_samples=recording.n_samples,
        window_seconds=window_length,
        step_seconds=step_length,
        threshold=threshold,
        windows=tuple(window_results),
        model_name=fusion.name,
        warnings=tuple(dict.fromkeys(warnings)),
    )

docs.text:
Read a numeric CSV/TSV where rows are samples and columns are channels.

Source code in src/biosqi/io.py 
def read_csv(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    sample_rate: float,
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.GENERIC,
) -> Recording:
    """Read a numeric CSV/TSV where rows are samples and columns are channels."""

    source = Path(path)
    with source.open("r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
        sample = handle.read(8192)
        handle.seek(0)
        try:
            dialect = csv.Sniffer().sniff(sample, delimiters=",;\t")
        except csv.Error:
            dialect = csv.excel
        rows = list(csv.reader(handle, dialect))
    rows = [row for row in rows if row and any(cell.strip() for cell in row)]
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("CSV file is empty")

    def numeric(row: list[str]) -> bool:
        try:
            [float(cell.strip()) for cell in row]
        except ValueError:
            return False
        return True

    has_header = not numeric(rows[0])
    names = tuple(cell.strip() or f"ch{i}" for i, cell in enumerate(rows[0])) if has_header else ()
    body = rows[1:] if has_header else rows
    width = len(body[0]) if body else 0
    if width == 0 or any(len(row) != width for row in body):
        raise ValueError("CSV rows must have a consistent, non-zero column count")
    if names and len(names) != width:
        raise ValueError("CSV header and data column counts differ")
    try:
        data = np.asarray([[float(cell.strip()) for cell in row] for row in body], dtype=np.float64)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError("CSV contains non-numeric data") from exc
    return Recording(data.T, sample_rate, names, signal_type, str(source))

def read_edf(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.GENERIC,
) -> Recording:
    """Read EDF/BDF via ``pyedflib``; channels must share a sample rate."""

    pyedflib = _optional_import("pyedflib", "data")
    source = Path(path)
    reader = pyedflib.EdfReader(str(source))
    try:
        rates = np.asarray(reader.getSampleFrequencies(), dtype=np.float64)
        if rates.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("EDF file contains no channels")
        if not np.allclose(rates, rates[0]):
            raise ValueError(
                "EDF channels have different sample rates; select or resample channels first"
            )
        data = np.vstack([reader.readSignal(index) for index in range(reader.signals_in_file)])
        names = tuple(str(name).strip() for name in reader.getSignalLabels())
        metadata = {"physical_dimensions": list(reader.getPhysicalDimensions())}
    finally:
        reader.close()
    return Recording(data, float(rates[0]), names, signal_type, str(source), metadata)

docs.title: read_numpy(path, *, sample_rate=None, signal_type=SignalType.GENERIC, channel_axis=0)
docs.text:
Read .npy or .npz arrays.

An NPZ may store data, sample_rate (or fs), and channel_names. Plain NPY inputs require sample_rate.

Source code in src/biosqi/io.py 
def read_numpy(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    sample_rate: float | None = None,
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.GENERIC,
    channel_axis: int = 0,
) -> Recording:
    """Read ``.npy`` or ``.npz`` arrays.

    An NPZ may store ``data``, ``sample_rate`` (or ``fs``), and ``channel_names``.
    Plain NPY inputs require ``sample_rate``.
    """

    source = Path(path)
    loaded = np.load(source, allow_pickle=False)
    names: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if isinstance(loaded, np.lib.npyio.NpzFile):
        try:
            keys = loaded.files
            data_key = "data" if "data" in keys else keys[0] if keys else None
            if data_key is None:
                raise ValueError("NPZ archive contains no arrays")
            data = np.asarray(loaded[data_key])
            if sample_rate is None:
                for key in ("sample_rate", "fs"):
                    if key in keys:
                        sample_rate = float(np.asarray(loaded[key]).reshape(-1)[0])
                        break
            if "channel_names" in keys:
                names = tuple(str(name) for name in np.asarray(loaded["channel_names"]).tolist())
            metadata["npz_key"] = data_key
        finally:
            loaded.close()
    else:
        data = np.asarray(loaded)
    if sample_rate is None:
        raise ValueError("sample_rate is required unless stored in an NPZ archive")
    oriented = _orient(data, channel_axis)
    return Recording(oriented, sample_rate, names, signal_type, str(source), metadata)

docs.title: read_recording(path, *, sample_rate=None, signal_type=SignalType.GENERIC, channel_axis=0)
docs.text:
Dispatch to a reader based on the source suffix.

Source code in src/biosqi/io.py 
def read_recording(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    sample_rate: float | None = None,
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.GENERIC,
    channel_axis: int = 0,
) -> Recording:
    """Dispatch to a reader based on the source suffix."""

    source = Path(path)
    suffix = source.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in {".npy", ".npz"}:
        return read_numpy(
            source,
            sample_rate=sample_rate,
            signal_type=signal_type,
            channel_axis=channel_axis,
        )
    if suffix in {".csv", ".tsv", ".txt"}:
        if sample_rate is None:
            raise ValueError("sample_rate is required for delimited text files")
        return read_csv(source, sample_rate=sample_rate, signal_type=signal_type)
    if suffix in {".edf", ".bdf"}:
        return read_edf(source, signal_type=signal_type)
    if suffix in {".hea", ".dat"} or not suffix:
        return read_wfdb(source, signal_type=signal_type)
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported input format: {suffix or '<none>'}")

def read_wfdb(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.ECG,
) -> Recording:
    """Read a WFDB record using the optional ``wfdb`` package."""

    wfdb = _optional_import("wfdb", "data")
    source = Path(path)
    record_name = str(source.with_suffix("")) if source.suffix in {".hea", ".dat"} else str(source)
    record = wfdb.rdrecord(record_name)
    data = np.asarray(record.p_signal, dtype=np.float64).T
    names = tuple(str(name) for name in getattr(record, "sig_name", ()))
    metadata = {"units": list(getattr(record, "units", ()))}
    return Recording(data, float(record.fs), names, signal_type, str(source), metadata)

def get_profile(signal_type: SignalType | str) -> SignalProfile:
    """Return the profile for an enum or case-insensitive string."""

    try:
        kind = (
            signal_type if isinstance(signal_type, SignalType) else SignalType(signal_type.lower())
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        supported = ", ".join(item.value for item in SignalType)
        raise ValueError(
            f"unsupported signal type {signal_type!r}; choose from {supported}"
        ) from exc
    return PROFILES[kind]

def iter_windows(
    recording: Recording,
    window_seconds: float,
    step_seconds: float,
    *,
    include_partial: bool = True,
) -> Iterator[SignalWindow]:
    """Yield channel-major views over a recording in ascending sample order."""

    bounds = window_bounds(
        recording.n_samples,
        recording.sample_rate,
        window_seconds,
        step_seconds,
        include_partial=include_partial,
    )
    for index, (start, stop) in enumerate(bounds):
        yield SignalWindow(
            index=index,
            start=start,
            stop=stop,
            data=recording.data[:, start:stop],
            sample_rate=recording.sample_rate,
        )

docs.text:
Convert seconds to samples using stable half-up rounding.

Source code in src/biosqi/windowing.py 
def seconds_to_samples(seconds: float, sample_rate: float, *, name: str = "duration") -> int:
    """Convert seconds to samples using stable half-up rounding."""

    if not np.isfinite(seconds) or seconds <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite and positive")
    if not np.isfinite(sample_rate) or sample_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("sample_rate must be finite and positive")
    samples = int(np.floor(seconds * sample_rate + 0.5))
    if samples < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} is shorter than one sample")
    return samples

docs.title: window_bounds(n_samples, sample_rate, window_seconds, step_seconds, *, include_partial=True)
docs.text:
Return deterministic half-open bounds, without padding or duplicated tails.

Source code in src/biosqi/windowing.py 
def window_bounds(
    n_samples: int,
    sample_rate: float,
    window_seconds: float,
    step_seconds: float,
    *,
    include_partial: bool = True,
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]:
    """Return deterministic half-open bounds, without padding or duplicated tails."""

    if n_samples < 0:
        raise ValueError("n_samples cannot be negative")
    size = seconds_to_samples(window_seconds, sample_rate, name="window_seconds")
    step = seconds_to_samples(step_seconds, sample_rate, name="step_seconds")
    if n_samples == 0:
        return ()
    if n_samples <= size:
        return ((0, n_samples),) if include_partial or n_samples == size else ()

    starts = list(range(0, n_samples - size + 1, step))
    bounds = [(start, start + size) for start in starts]
    next_start = (starts[-1] + step) if starts else 0
    if include_partial and bounds[-1][1] < n_samples and next_start < n_samples:
        bounds.append((next_start, n_samples))
    return tuple(bounds)

Numerically robust signal-quality indicators.

Normalized qualities and artifact thresholds in this module are transparent engineering heuristics. They are not clinical decision limits and should be recalibrated on a labelled, task-representative dataset.

docs.title: baseline_wander_ratio(values, sample_rate, baseline_band, physiological_band)
docs.text:
Measure baseline-band power relative to physiological-band power.

Baseline power ratios are motivated by Clifford et al., Physiol. Meas. 33(9), 2012. Profile bands and the ratio-to-score transform are heuristic.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def baseline_wander_ratio(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    baseline_band: tuple[float, float],
    physiological_band: tuple[float, float],
) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Measure baseline-band power relative to physiological-band power.

    Baseline power ratios are motivated by Clifford et al., Physiol. Meas.
    33(9), 2012. Profile bands and the ratio-to-score transform are heuristic.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("baseline_wander_ratio", "baseline_wander", "too few finite samples")
    frequencies, power = _welch(x, sample_rate)
    baseline = _band_power(frequencies, power, baseline_band)
    physiological = _band_power(frequencies, power, physiological_band)
    ratio = baseline / max(baseline + physiological, _EPS)
    return IndicatorResult(
        "baseline_wander_ratio",
        ratio,
        float(np.clip((1.0 - ratio) * finite_fraction, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "baseline_wander",
        {"baseline_power": baseline, "physiological_power": physiological},
    )

docs.title: beat_agreement_template(values, sample_rate, signal_type, rate_bpm)
docs.text:
Compare two independent beat detectors and beat-template morphology.

Detector agreement as a quality concept follows Clifford et al., Physiol. Meas. 33(9), 2012; template correlation follows Orphanidou et al., IEEE J. Biomed. Health Inform. 19(3), 2015. The 150 ms tolerance and equal score weighting are explicit heuristics, not clinical thresholds.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def beat_agreement_template(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    signal_type: SignalType,
    rate_bpm: tuple[float, float] | None,
) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Compare two independent beat detectors and beat-template morphology.

    Detector agreement as a quality concept follows Clifford et al., Physiol.
    Meas. 33(9), 2012; template correlation follows Orphanidou et al., IEEE
    J. Biomed. Health Inform. 19(3), 2015. The 150 ms tolerance and equal score
    weighting are explicit heuristics, not clinical thresholds.
    """

    if signal_type not in {SignalType.ECG, SignalType.PPG} or rate_bpm is None:
        return _invalid("beat_agreement_template", "beat_inconsistency", "not applicable")
    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values, minimum=max(16, int(sample_rate)))
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("beat_agreement_template", "beat_inconsistency", "window is too short")
    first = detect_peaks_prominence(x, sample_rate, signal_type, rate_bpm)
    second = detect_peaks_energy(x, sample_rate, signal_type, rate_bpm)
    tolerance = max(1, round(0.15 * sample_rate))
    agreement = _beat_agreement(first, second, tolerance)
    template = _template_correlation(x, first, max(1, round(0.2 * sample_rate)))
    template_quality = max(0.0, template)
    quality = finite_fraction * (0.6 * agreement + 0.4 * template_quality)
    return IndicatorResult(
        "beat_agreement_template",
        agreement,
        float(np.clip(quality, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "beat_inconsistency",
        {
            "prominence_peak_count": int(first.size),
            "energy_peak_count": int(second.size),
            "agreement_f1": agreement,
            "template_correlation": template,
            "tolerance_ms": 1000.0 * tolerance / sample_rate,
        },
    )

docs.title: clipping_flatline_rms(values)
docs.text:
Measure clipping, flat-line occupancy, and RMS amplitude.

Flat-line and saturation checks are common in Li et al., Physiol. Meas. 29(1), 2008. Without ADC limits, clipping is inferred from repeated extrema; the 1% tolerance and score weights are dataset-agnostic heuristics.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def clipping_flatline_rms(values: npt.ArrayLike) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Measure clipping, flat-line occupancy, and RMS amplitude.

    Flat-line and saturation checks are common in Li et al., Physiol. Meas.
    29(1), 2008. Without ADC limits, clipping is inferred from repeated extrema;
    the 1% tolerance and score weights are dataset-agnostic heuristics.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("clipping_flatline_rms", "amplitude_failure", "too few finite samples")
    span = float(np.ptp(x))
    scale = max(span, float(np.nanstd(x)), _EPS)
    tolerance = max(scale * 1e-6, _EPS)
    at_minimum = np.abs(x - np.min(x)) <= tolerance
    at_maximum = np.abs(x - np.max(x)) <= tolerance
    clipping = float(np.mean(at_minimum | at_maximum))
    differences = np.abs(np.diff(x))
    flatline = float(np.mean(differences <= max(scale * 1e-5, _EPS)))
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(x - np.mean(x)))))
    dynamic = 0.0 if span <= _EPS else 1.0
    quality = dynamic * finite_fraction * np.exp(-8.0 * clipping - 12.0 * flatline)
    return IndicatorResult(
        "clipping_flatline_rms",
        rms,
        float(np.clip(quality, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "amplitude_failure",
        {"clipping_fraction": clipping, "flatline_fraction": flatline, "rms": rms},
    )

def compute_indicators(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    profile: SignalProfile,
) -> tuple[IndicatorResult, ...]:
    """Compute all applicable indicators without allowing one failure to abort a window."""

    computations: tuple[Callable[[], IndicatorResult], ...] = (
        lambda: spectral_band_power_ratio(values, sample_rate, profile.physiological_band),
        lambda: spectral_entropy(values, sample_rate),
        lambda: line_noise_ratio(values, sample_rate),
        lambda: clipping_flatline_rms(values),
        lambda: baseline_wander_ratio(
            values, sample_rate, profile.baseline_band, profile.physiological_band
        ),
        lambda: distribution_shape(values),
        lambda: periodicity_autocorrelation(values, sample_rate, profile.expected_rate_bpm),
        lambda: beat_agreement_template(
            values, sample_rate, profile.signal_type, profile.expected_rate_bpm
        ),
    )
    results: list[IndicatorResult] = []
    for computation in computations:
        try:
            results.append(computation())
        except (ValueError, FloatingPointError, OverflowError) as exc:
            name = getattr(computation, "__name__", "indicator")
            results.append(_invalid(name, "numerical_failure", str(exc)))
    return tuple(results)

docs.title: detect_peaks_energy(values, sample_rate, signal_type, rate_bpm)
docs.text:
Detect beats from derivative energy and adaptive local maxima.

Squared derivative integration follows Pan and Tompkins, IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng. BME-32(3), 1985. Parameters are simplified for quality agreement and must not be treated as a diagnostic QRS detector.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def detect_peaks_energy(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    signal_type: SignalType,
    rate_bpm: tuple[float, float],
) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
    """Detect beats from derivative energy and adaptive local maxima.

    Squared derivative integration follows Pan and Tompkins, IEEE Trans.
    Biomed. Eng. BME-32(3), 1985. Parameters are simplified for quality
    agreement and must not be treated as a diagnostic QRS detector.
    """

    x, _ = _prepare(values, minimum=16)
    if x is None:
        return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int64)
    band = (5.0, 18.0) if signal_type == SignalType.ECG else (0.5, 8.0)
    filtered = _bandpass(x, sample_rate, band)
    derivative_energy = np.square(np.gradient(filtered))
    width = max(1, round(sample_rate * (0.12 if signal_type == SignalType.ECG else 0.20)))
    integrated = np.convolve(derivative_energy, np.ones(width) / width, mode="same")
    distance = max(1, int(np.floor(60.0 * sample_rate / rate_bpm[1])))
    threshold = float(np.median(integrated) + 1.5 * stats.median_abs_deviation(integrated))
    candidates, _ = signal.find_peaks(integrated, distance=distance, height=threshold)
    radius = max(1, round(0.12 * sample_rate))
    refined: list[int] = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        start, stop = max(0, candidate - radius), min(x.size, candidate + radius + 1)
        local = np.abs(filtered[start:stop])
        refined.append(start + int(np.argmax(local)))
    return np.asarray(sorted(set(refined)), dtype=np.int64)

def detect_peaks_prominence(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    signal_type: SignalType,
    rate_bpm: tuple[float, float],
) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
    """Detect beats using bandpass amplitude and robust prominence.

    This intentionally simple detector is independent of the energy detector.
    Its filtering/peak-search structure is inspired by Elgendi, PLoS ONE 8(10),
    2013 for PPG and Hamilton, Comput. Cardiol., 2002 for ECG.
    """

    x, _ = _prepare(values, minimum=16)
    if x is None:
        return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int64)
    band = (5.0, 18.0) if signal_type == SignalType.ECG else (0.5, 8.0)
    filtered = _bandpass(x, sample_rate, band)
    distance = max(1, int(np.floor(60.0 * sample_rate / rate_bpm[1])))
    prominence = max(float(stats.median_abs_deviation(filtered, scale="normal")), _EPS) * 0.8
    positive, properties = signal.find_peaks(filtered, distance=distance, prominence=prominence)
    negative, negative_properties = signal.find_peaks(
        -filtered, distance=distance, prominence=prominence
    )
    positive_strength = float(np.sum(properties.get("prominences", ())))
    negative_strength = float(np.sum(negative_properties.get("prominences", ())))
    selected = positive if positive_strength >= negative_strength else negative
    return np.asarray(selected, dtype=np.int64)

docs.text:
Return skewness and Pearson kurtosis with a conservative morphology score.

Orphanidou et al., IEEE J. Biomed. Health Inform. 19(3), 2015 discuss statistical ECG quality features. No universal target distribution exists; the score only down-weights very extreme shape statistics.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def distribution_shape(values: npt.ArrayLike) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Return skewness and Pearson kurtosis with a conservative morphology score.

    Orphanidou et al., IEEE J. Biomed. Health Inform. 19(3), 2015 discuss
    statistical ECG quality features. No universal target distribution exists;
    the score only down-weights very extreme shape statistics.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("distribution_shape", "morphology_outlier", "too few finite samples")
    if float(np.ptp(x)) <= _EPS:
        return _invalid("distribution_shape", "morphology_outlier", "constant or degenerate signal")
    skewness = float(stats.skew(x, bias=False))
    kurtosis = float(stats.kurtosis(x, fisher=False, bias=False))
    if not np.isfinite(skewness) or not np.isfinite(kurtosis):
        return _invalid("distribution_shape", "morphology_outlier", "constant or degenerate signal")
    penalty = max(0.0, abs(skewness) - 2.0) + 0.25 * max(0.0, kurtosis - 12.0)
    quality = np.exp(-penalty) * finite_fraction
    return IndicatorResult(
        "distribution_shape",
        kurtosis,
        float(np.clip(quality, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "morphology_outlier",
        {"skewness": skewness, "pearson_kurtosis": kurtosis},
    )

docs.title: line_noise_ratio(values, sample_rate)
docs.text:
Measure 50/60 Hz power relative to nearby high-frequency power.

Power-line interference assessment is consistent with Clifford et al., Physiol. Meas. 33(9), 2012. The 1 Hz bands and exponential score mapping are transparent engineering choices, not validated clinical thresholds.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def line_noise_ratio(values: npt.ArrayLike, sample_rate: float) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Measure 50/60 Hz power relative to nearby high-frequency power.

    Power-line interference assessment is consistent with Clifford et al.,
    Physiol. Meas. 33(9), 2012. The 1 Hz bands and exponential score mapping
    are transparent engineering choices, not validated clinical thresholds.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("line_noise_ratio", "line_noise", "too few finite samples")
    frequencies, power = _welch(x, sample_rate)
    nyquist = sample_rate / 2
    candidates = [frequency for frequency in (50.0, 60.0) if frequency + 1 <= nyquist]
    if not candidates:
        return _invalid("line_noise_ratio", "line_noise", "sample rate cannot resolve 50/60 Hz")
    ratios: dict[float, float] = {}
    for frequency in candidates:
        tone = _band_power(frequencies, power, (frequency - 1.0, frequency + 1.0))
        neighborhood = _band_power(frequencies, power, (frequency - 5.0, frequency + 5.0))
        ratios[frequency] = tone / max(neighborhood - tone, _EPS)
    mains, ratio = max(ratios.items(), key=lambda item: item[1])
    quality = float(np.exp(-2.0 * ratio) * finite_fraction)
    return IndicatorResult(
        "line_noise_ratio",
        ratio,
        float(np.clip(quality, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "line_noise",
        {"dominant_mains_hz": mains, "ratios": str(ratios)},
    )

docs.title: periodicity_autocorrelation(values, sample_rate, rate_bpm)
docs.text:
Find the strongest normalized autocorrelation at plausible beat lags.

Autocorrelation SQIs follow the periodicity principle in Li et al., Physiol. Meas. 29(1), 2008. Plausible rate bounds come from the selected profile and are broad quality-analysis assumptions, not diagnostic limits.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def periodicity_autocorrelation(
    values: npt.ArrayLike,
    sample_rate: float,
    rate_bpm: tuple[float, float] | None,
) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Find the strongest normalized autocorrelation at plausible beat lags.

    Autocorrelation SQIs follow the periodicity principle in Li et al.,
    Physiol. Meas. 29(1), 2008. Plausible rate bounds come from the selected
    profile and are broad quality-analysis assumptions, not diagnostic limits.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values, minimum=16)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("periodicity_autocorrelation", "aperiodicity", "too few finite samples")
    x = np.asarray(signal.detrend(x), dtype=np.float64)
    variance = float(np.dot(x, x))
    if variance <= _EPS:
        return _invalid("periodicity_autocorrelation", "aperiodicity", "constant signal")
    correlation = signal.correlate(x, x, mode="full", method="fft")[x.size - 1 :] / variance
    if rate_bpm is None:
        minimum_lag = max(1, round(0.25 * sample_rate))
        maximum_lag = min(x.size - 1, round(2.0 * sample_rate))
    else:
        minimum_lag = max(1, int(np.floor(60.0 * sample_rate / rate_bpm[1])))
        maximum_lag = min(x.size - 1, int(np.ceil(60.0 * sample_rate / rate_bpm[0])))
    if maximum_lag <= minimum_lag:
        return _invalid("periodicity_autocorrelation", "aperiodicity", "window is too short")
    section = correlation[minimum_lag : maximum_lag + 1]
    relative_lag = int(np.argmax(section))
    peak = float(section[relative_lag])
    lag = minimum_lag + relative_lag
    quality = np.clip(max(peak, 0.0) * finite_fraction, 0.0, 1.0)
    return IndicatorResult(
        "periodicity_autocorrelation",
        peak,
        float(quality),
        "aperiodicity",
        {"lag_samples": lag, "rate_bpm": 60.0 * sample_rate / lag},
    )

docs.text:
Return in-band/total spectral power.

The Welch estimator follows Welch, IEEE Trans. Audio Electroacoustics 15(2), 1967. Band limits are profile defaults, not universal physiology.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def spectral_band_power_ratio(
    values: npt.ArrayLike, sample_rate: float, band: tuple[float, float]
) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Return in-band/total spectral power.

    The Welch estimator follows Welch, IEEE Trans. Audio Electroacoustics
    15(2), 1967. Band limits are profile defaults, not universal physiology.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("spectral_power_ratio", "broadband_noise", "too few finite samples")
    frequencies, power = _welch(x, sample_rate)
    nyquist = sample_rate / 2
    effective_band = (max(0.0, band[0]), min(band[1], nyquist))
    total = _band_power(frequencies, power, (max(0.01, frequencies[1]), nyquist))
    ratio = _band_power(frequencies, power, effective_band) / max(total, _EPS)
    quality = float(np.clip(ratio * finite_fraction, 0.0, 1.0))
    return IndicatorResult(
        "spectral_power_ratio",
        ratio,
        quality,
        "broadband_noise",
        {"band_low_hz": effective_band[0], "band_high_hz": effective_band[1]},
    )

docs.title: spectral_entropy(values, sample_rate)
docs.text:
Estimate normalized spectral entropy.

Spectral entropy as an SQI follows the information-theoretic approach used by Zhang et al., IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng. 62(9), 2015. The quality mapping, centered on moderate entropy, is heuristic because either extreme can be poor depending on signal family.

Source code in src/biosqi/indicators.py 
def spectral_entropy(values: npt.ArrayLike, sample_rate: float) -> IndicatorResult:
    """Estimate normalized spectral entropy.

    Spectral entropy as an SQI follows the information-theoretic approach used
    by Zhang et al., IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng. 62(9), 2015. The quality mapping,
    centered on moderate entropy, is heuristic because either extreme can be
    poor depending on signal family.
    """

    x, finite_fraction = _prepare(values)
    if x is None:
        return _invalid("spectral_entropy", "spectral_disorder", "too few finite samples")
    _, power = _welch(x, sample_rate)
    mass = power / max(float(np.sum(power)), _EPS)
    entropy = -float(np.sum(mass * np.log2(mass + _EPS))) / max(np.log2(mass.size), _EPS)
    quality = 1.0 - abs(entropy - 0.6) / 0.6
    return IndicatorResult(
        "spectral_entropy",
        entropy,
        float(np.clip(quality * finite_fraction, 0.0, 1.0)),
        "spectral_disorder",
        {"interpretation": "extreme values are penalized heuristically"},
    )

Serializable logistic model followed by piecewise-linear isotonic calibration.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FusionModel:
    """Serializable logistic model followed by piecewise-linear isotonic calibration."""

    name: str
    features: tuple[str, ...]
    weights: tuple[float, ...]
    intercept: float
    calibration_x: tuple[float, ...] = (0.0, 1.0)
    calibration_y: tuple[float, ...] = (0.0, 1.0)
    missing_value: float = 0.5
    provenance: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.features or len(self.features) != len(self.weights):
            raise ValueError("features and weights must be non-empty and equally sized")
        if len(self.calibration_x) != len(self.calibration_y) or len(self.calibration_x) < 2:
            raise ValueError("calibration arrays must have equal length and at least two points")
        if any(right < left for left, right in pairwise(self.calibration_x)):
            raise ValueError("calibration_x must be nondecreasing")
        if any(right < left for left, right in pairwise(self.calibration_y)):
            raise ValueError("calibration_y must be nondecreasing")

    def predict(self, indicators: tuple[IndicatorResult, ...]) -> FusionOutput:
        """Fuse valid indicator qualities; missing features use the documented neutral value."""

        qualities = {
            indicator.name: indicator.quality
            for indicator in indicators
            if indicator.valid and indicator.quality is not None
        }
        contributions: dict[str, float] = {}
        logit = self.intercept
        for feature, weight in zip(self.features, self.weights, strict=True):
            value = float(qualities.get(feature, self.missing_value))
            contribution = weight * value
            contributions[feature] = contribution
            logit += contribution
        raw = _sigmoid(logit)
        calibrated = float(
            np.interp(
                raw,
                np.asarray(self.calibration_x),
                np.asarray(self.calibration_y),
                left=self.calibration_y[0],
                right=self.calibration_y[-1],
            )
        )
        return FusionOutput(raw, float(np.clip(calibrated, 0.0, 1.0)), contributions)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "features": list(self.features),
            "weights": list(self.weights),
            "intercept": self.intercept,
            "calibration": {"x": list(self.calibration_x), "y": list(self.calibration_y)},
            "missing_value": self.missing_value,
            "provenance": self.provenance,
        }

    def save(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> FusionModel:
        calibration = payload.get("calibration", {})
        return cls(
            name=str(payload["name"]),
            features=tuple(str(item) for item in payload["features"]),
            weights=tuple(float(item) for item in payload["weights"]),
            intercept=float(payload["intercept"]),
            calibration_x=tuple(float(item) for item in calibration.get("x", (0.0, 1.0))),
            calibration_y=tuple(float(item) for item in calibration.get("y", (0.0, 1.0))),
            missing_value=float(payload.get("missing_value", 0.5)),
            provenance=dict(payload.get("provenance", {})),
        )

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> FusionModel:
        payload = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise ValueError("model JSON root must be an object")
        return cls.from_dict(payload)

docs.text:
Fit logistic fusion with isotonic calibration on out-of-fold predictions.

Source code in src/biosqi/fusion.py 
def fit_fusion_model(
    features: npt.ArrayLike,
    labels: npt.ArrayLike,
    feature_names: tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    name: str = "fitted-logistic-isotonic",
    random_state: int = 0,
) -> FusionModel:
    """Fit logistic fusion with isotonic calibration on out-of-fold predictions."""

    x = np.asarray(features, dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(labels, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1)
    if x.ndim != 2 or x.shape[1] != len(feature_names):
        raise ValueError("features must be a 2D array matching feature_names")
    if x.shape[0] != y.size or y.size < 4:
        raise ValueError("labels must match rows and contain at least four observations")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(x)):
        raise ValueError("training features must be finite")
    unique = np.unique(y)
    if not np.array_equal(unique, np.array([0, 1])):
        raise ValueError("labels must contain both binary classes 0 and 1")
    class_counts = np.bincount(y, minlength=2)
    if int(class_counts.min()) < 2:
        raise ValueError("each class needs at least two observations for calibration")
    folds = min(5, int(class_counts.min()))
    splitter = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=folds, shuffle=True, random_state=random_state)
    logistic = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, class_weight="balanced", random_state=random_state)
    raw = cross_val_predict(
        logistic,
        x,
        y,
        cv=splitter,
        method="predict_proba",
    )[:, 1]
    calibrator = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds="clip")
    calibrator.fit(raw, y)
    logistic.fit(x, y)
    calibration_x = tuple(float(item) for item in calibrator.X_thresholds_)
    calibration_y = tuple(float(item) for item in calibrator.y_thresholds_)
    return FusionModel(
        name=name,
        features=feature_names,
        weights=tuple(float(item) for item in logistic.coef_[0]),
        intercept=float(logistic.intercept_[0]),
        calibration_x=calibration_x,
        calibration_y=calibration_y,
    )

Aggregate 1 - quality by artifact using absolute model weights.

Values are relative diagnostic severities, not probabilities. Invalid or non-applicable indicators are omitted instead of being silently called bad.

Source code in src/biosqi/attribution.py 
def attribute_artifacts(
    indicators: tuple[IndicatorResult, ...],
    model: FusionModel,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Aggregate ``1 - quality`` by artifact using absolute model weights.

    Values are relative diagnostic severities, not probabilities. Invalid or
    non-applicable indicators are omitted instead of being silently called bad.
    """

    weights = dict(zip(model.features, model.weights, strict=True))
    weighted_deficit: defaultdict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    total_weight: defaultdict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    for indicator in indicators:
        if not indicator.valid or indicator.quality is None:
            continue
        weight = abs(weights.get(indicator.name, 1.0))
        weighted_deficit[indicator.artifact] += weight * (1.0 - indicator.quality)
        total_weight[indicator.artifact] += weight
    severities = {
        artifact: float(np.clip(deficit / total_weight[artifact], 0.0, 1.0))
        for artifact, deficit in weighted_deficit.items()
        if total_weight[artifact] > 0
    }
    return dict(sorted(severities.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0])))

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Recording:
    """A sampled, channel-major biomedical recording."""

    data: FloatArray
    sample_rate: float
    channel_names: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    signal_type: SignalType = SignalType.GENERIC
    source: str | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        data = np.asarray(self.data, dtype=np.float64)
        if data.ndim == 1:
            data = data[np.newaxis, :]
        if data.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("recording data must be one- or two-dimensional")
        if data.shape[0] < 1:
            raise ValueError("recording must contain at least one channel")
        if not np.isfinite(self.sample_rate) or self.sample_rate <= 0:
            raise ValueError("sample_rate must be finite and positive")
        signal_type = (
            self.signal_type
            if isinstance(self.signal_type, SignalType)
            else SignalType(str(self.signal_type).lower())
        )
        names = self.channel_names or tuple(f"ch{i}" for i in range(data.shape[0]))
        if len(names) != data.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("channel_names must match the channel count")
        object.__setattr__(self, "data", data)
        object.__setattr__(self, "channel_names", tuple(names))
        object.__setattr__(self, "signal_type", signal_type)

    @property
    def n_channels(self) -> int:
        return int(self.data.shape[0])

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        return int(self.data.shape[1])

    @property
    def duration(self) -> float:
        return self.n_samples / self.sample_rate

docs.title: Signal-quality indicators
docs.text: Every indicator returns a raw value, normalized quality in [0, 1], an artifact family, and diagnostic evidence. Thresholds are profile-specific engineering priors and are superseded by fitted fusion weights.

docs.title: Spectral power ratio
docs.text: Compares power in the profile’s expected physiological band with total power. Welch’s estimator is used for sufficiently long windows. This is related to the pSQI family described by Clifford et al. (2012).

docs.title: Spectral entropy
docs.text: Computes normalized Shannon entropy of the power spectral density. Extremely concentrated or diffuse spectra can both be implausible; profile thresholds map the raw value to quality without hiding it.

docs.title: Mains interference
docs.text: Measures power near 50 or 60 Hz and harmonics relative to neighboring or total power. The analysis tests the configured mains frequency and reports the evidence used.

docs.title: Clipping, flatline, and amplitude
docs.text: Detects repeated samples near observed rails, long runs with negligible first-difference, and implausible RMS. Because recording units differ by hardware, amplitude evidence is treated cautiously unless the profile supplies meaningful bounds.

docs.title: Baseline wander
docs.text: Measures low-frequency power beneath the profile cutoff relative to total power after removing the mean. It is evidence of drift or motion, not proof of the physical source.

docs.title: Distribution shape
docs.text: Skewness (sSQI) and kurtosis (kSQI) summarize waveform shape. These are weak indicators individually and receive modest fusion weight.

docs.title: Periodicity and beat agreement
docs.text: Autocorrelation peak prominence estimates quasi-periodic consistency. For ECG and PPG, two independent peak detectors are compared using tolerance-matched F1 agreement (bSQI), and aligned beat shapes are compared with their robust template.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Clifford, G. D., Lopez, D., Li, Q., & Rezek, I. (2012). Signal quality indices and data fusion for determining clinical acceptability of electrocardiograms. Physiological Measurement, 33(9), 1419–1433.
  • Li, Q., Mark, R. G., & Clifford, G. D. (2008). Robust heart rate estimation from multiple asynchronous noisy sources using signal quality indices and a Kalman filter. Physiological Measurement, 29(1), 15–32.
  • Moody, G. B., Muldrow, W. E., & Mark, R. G. (1984). A noise stress test for arrhythmia detectors. Computers in Cardiology, 11, 381–384.
  • Silva, I., Moody, G. B., & Celi, L. (2011). Improving the quality of ECGs collected using mobile phones: the PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2011. Computing in Cardiology, 38, 273–276.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
1. A reader converts the source into a channel-major float64 recording and preserves sampling rate and channel names.
  2. Deterministic half-open windows are generated in sample coordinates. No sample is silently interpolated.
  3. Every channel is evaluated independently. Undefined indicators are marked unavailable with a reason instead of being converted to a perfect or failed score.
  4. Normalized indicator qualities are fused by logistic regression.
  5. Raw probabilities pass through a monotone isotonic calibration map learned from out-of-fold predictions.
  6. Channel scores are aggregated by median. Artifact severities use the conservative maximum across channels.

docs.title: What “calibrated” means
docs.text:
Calibration is population-specific. In the released ECG model, logistic weights are fitted using all labeled records from PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2011 Set A. The isotonic map is fitted to predictions produced when each record was held outside its training fold. This prevents the calibrator from seeing in-sample predictions.

A score near 0.8 therefore means “among similar Set A recordings receiving this score, approximately 80% were labeled acceptable,” subject to sampling error and dataset shift. It does not mean the waveform is 80% clean, nor does it imply clinical safety.

docs.title: Missing evidence
docs.text: Some SQIs are meaningful only for particular signal families. Beat-template agreement, for example, is appropriate for ECG/PPG but not generic EEG. Missing indicator values use the model’s documented neutral value, and the analysis report records a warning. The library never fills missing waveform samples before calculating an SQI.

docs.title: Artifact attribution
docs.text: Attribution is evidence-based and intentionally multi-label. A window may show both line interference and clipping. Each artifact severity is a transparent function of one or more normalized SQIs; it is not a claim that the physical cause has been proven. The raw SQIs remain available for inspection.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
Run the quick benchmark:

uv run python benchmarks/run_all.py --quick

The release benchmark omits --quick, downloads all public labeled records, performs nested cross-validation, writes benchmarks/results/results.json, fits the packaged model, and replaces the generated README metric block.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install "biosqi[data,ui]"

The base package supports NumPy and delimited-text inputs. The data extra adds WFDB and EDF/BDF readers; ui adds the local FastAPI dashboard.

docs.title: Open the dashboard
docs.text:
biosqi view

The browser communicates only with a server bound to localhost. Uploaded recordings are processed in memory and are not sent to an external service.

docs.title: Score from the command line
docs.text:
biosqi score recording.csv \
  --sample-rate 250 \
  --signal-type ecg \
  --window 10 \
  --threshold 0.70 \
  --output result.json

Generate a self-contained report or export the usability mask:

biosqi report recording.npz --signal-type ppg --output report.html
biosqi mask recording.npz --signal-type ppg --output mask.csv

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
from biosqi.analysis import analyze
from biosqi.io import read_recording
from biosqi.types import SignalType

recording = read_recording(
    "recording.npz",
    signal_type=SignalType.ECG,
)
result = analyze(recording, threshold=0.70)

print(result.scores)
print(result.mask)

For plain .npy, .csv, .tsv, or .txt inputs, provide the sample rate. NPZ archives may include data, sample_rate, and channel_names arrays.

docs.title: Before tagging
docs.text:
uv sync --extra dev
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy src/biosqi
uv run pytest
uv run python benchmarks/run_all.py
uv build

Confirm that benchmarks/results/results.json, both SVG plots, the README metric block, and src/biosqi/models/default.json changed in the same run. Inspect the generated model name and provenance before release.

Build the dashboard and verify the bundled assets:

cd frontend
npm ci
npm run test:run
npm run build
cd ..
biosqi view

docs.title: Cutting a release
docs.text:
1. Bump version in pyproject.toml, __version__ in src/biosqi/__init__.py, and version/date-released in CITATION.cff.
  2. Move the Unreleased entries in CHANGELOG.md under the new version.
  3. Commit, then tag and push:
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin main v0.2.0

The Release workflow then:

  1. checks that the tag matches the package version,
  2. builds the sdist and wheel,
  3. publishes them to PyPI via trusted publishing (GitHub environment pypi; no API token is stored), and
  4. creates the GitHub release with generated notes and the built files.

Zenodo archives every published GitHub release and mints a version DOI. The concept DOI in the README always resolves to the latest version.

Do not upload releases to Zenodo manually; the GitHub integration already creates a record for each release, and a manual upload would produce a separate, unrelated record.

docs.title: PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2011
docs.text:
Set A contains approximately 1,000 ten-second, 12-lead ECGs sampled at 500 Hz. Each recording was reviewed independently by 3–18 annotators. The benchmark uses the public acceptable and unacceptable lists; indeterminate records are excluded, matching the Challenge scoring policy.

Reported generalization metrics come from five stratified outer folds. Isotonic calibration is fitted using three inner folds within each outer training split. ROC AUC includes a deterministic 2,000-sample stratified bootstrap confidence interval. No score is reported for Set B or C because their reference labels are withheld.

docs.title: MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database
docs.text: The NSTDB test uses records 118 and 119 corrupted with real electrode-motion noise at 24, 18, 12, 6, 0, and ?6 dB SNR. It checks whether mean quality tracks increasing SNR across noisy intervals. This is a stress test of ordering, not an independent expert-label classification test.

docs.title: Synthetic corruption
docs.text:
The controlled harness injects baseline wander, mains interference, smoothed motion noise, electrode pops, clipping, and dropout into clean signals. For additive artifacts, noise is scaled to a requested SNR and measured again after injection. Every corruption includes an exact sample-level affected mask.

Synthetic data tests whether an algorithm reacts to a known perturbation. It does not substitute for validation on real acquisition failures.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Challenge 2011 contains short, mobile 12-lead ECG acquisitions. Results may not transfer to long-term Holter, ICU, wearable single-lead, PPG, or EEG.
  • Acceptability depends on the intended analysis. A segment adequate for heart rate may be inadequate for morphology.
  • Artifact attribution is an interpretable hypothesis derived from SQIs, not a causal diagnosis.
  • The PPG and EEG profiles are supported engineering configurations; only the ECG model receives the stated Challenge 2011 calibration.

Dataset licenses and provenance are recorded beside each downloaded cache.
